id: AT-AP-15 (start records without milliseconds, review of bcdaca6)
note: Review of bcdaca6: start records carry milliseconds only when Time::HiRes loads. A record without them names only the second the session started in (sessions::own_start coarse): rows from a later second are own by time; a row from that second is own only when it is a typed user row that follows one of this session's SessionStart hook rows (stamped in or after that second) with no older row between, so a copied row never counts and the launch prompt is not missed when the hook rows are there. Negatives: a typed row before the hook rows, an older row after the hook row, a SessionStart row from an earlier second, another hook's row, a sidechain's SessionStart row, a forkedFrom row; a millisecond record in the same second ends the window. The hook-driven pair writes the record through SessionStart with the no-milliseconds stamp forced (STORE_TEST_NO_HIRES) and with whatever the perl has: the answers are the same.
